quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Less Fresh Seafood] The catering company loses its contract with the hotel after switching suppliers, and within weeks, three separate reviews mention the seafood tasting noticeably less fresh than before.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the new supplier?
options: It may not provide seafood of the same quality as the previous one.
It has no connection to the reviews at all.
It only supplies desserts, not seafood.
It provides fresher seafood than the previous supplier.
quests.correctAnswer: It may not provide seafood of the same quality as the previous one.
quests.hint: Think about the timing between the supplier switch and the complaints about freshness.
quests.explanation: Reviews noting less fresh seafood right after the supplier switch suggest the new supplier may not match the previous one's quality.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [The Suggestion Box] The office's suggestion box, once ignored for months, fills up within a week after management begins publicly responding to each idea at the Monday meeting.
quests.question: What can be inferred about employees' earlier use of the suggestion box?
options: They may have doubted that their suggestions would be taken seriously.
They were fully satisfied with how suggestions were handled before.
The suggestion box was physically inaccessible before.
They never had any suggestions to offer.
quests.correctAnswer: They may have doubted that their suggestions would be taken seriously.
quests.hint: Think about what changed right before employees started using the box more, and what that reveals about their earlier hesitation.
quests.explanation: The box filling up only after management started responding publicly suggests employees may have previously doubted their suggestions would matter.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [The Same Lemon Cake] Every family recipe box that gets passed down includes a card for the same lemon cake, each written in a different relative's handwriting but with identical measurements.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the lemon cake recipe?
options: It is a recipe the family no longer uses.
It was only made once by a single relative.
It has changed significantly with each generation.
It has been carefully preserved and shared across generations.
quests.correctAnswer: It has been carefully preserved and shared across generations.
quests.hint: Think about what identical measurements, copied by different people over time, suggest about how carefully it was passed down.
quests.explanation: Identical measurements copied by different relatives suggest the recipe has been carefully preserved and passed down exactly as originally made.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [An Outdated Refill Call] The pharmacy's automated refill system calls Mrs. Osei twice about a prescription she stopped taking months ago, so she asks the pharmacist to update her file directly instead of relying on the app.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the automated system?
options: It is unrelated to her prescription history.
It was working exactly as it should.
It had not been updated with her current prescription information.
It successfully reflected all of her recent changes.
quests.correctAnswer: It had not been updated with her current prescription information.
quests.hint: Think about why the system would call about medication she is no longer taking.
quests.explanation: Calling about a discontinued prescription suggests the automated system had not been updated with Mrs. Osei's current information.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Trouble by Five O'Clock] The department store's self-checkout lines move quickly all afternoon, but by five o'clock, a staff member is assigned to stand beside them helping customer after customer with error messages.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the self-checkout machines in the late afternoon?
options: They only have problems in the morning.
They work perfectly with no issues all day.
They begin causing more problems for customers around that time.
They are turned off completely at five o'clock.
quests.correctAnswer: They begin causing more problems for customers around that time.
quests.hint: Think about why extra staff support would specifically be needed starting at that time of day.
quests.explanation: Needing a staff member to help with error messages starting at five o'clock suggests the machines begin causing more issues around that time, likely due to higher afternoon traffic.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Scrolling Before Bed] The fitness watch's sleep score consistently drops on nights Elias mentions scrolling on his phone in bed, compared to nights he reads a physical book instead.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the effect of phone use before bed?
options: It consistently improves his sleep score.
It has no measurable effect on his sleep.
It only affects how long he sleeps, not the quality.
It may be negatively affecting the quality of his sleep.
quests.correctAnswer: It may be negatively affecting the quality of his sleep.
quests.hint: Compare the sleep scores on the nights with each activity.
quests.explanation: Lower sleep scores specifically on nights with phone use, compared to reading, suggest screen time before bed may be affecting his sleep quality.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Two Different Seats] The airline's app shows Ingrid's seat as 14C, but the boarding pass printed at the counter lists 22A, and the gate agent asks her to keep the printed version instead.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the app's seating information?
options: It was correct, and the gate agent made an error.
Both documents show the exact same seat.
It may not reflect the most up-to-date assignment.
It is more accurate than the printed boarding pass.
quests.correctAnswer: It may not reflect the most up-to-date assignment.
quests.hint: Think about why the gate agent would specifically ask her to rely on the printed version instead.
quests.explanation: Being told to rely on the printed boarding pass, which differs from the app, suggests the app's seat information was outdated.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Standing-Room Office Hours] The professor's office hours used to be nearly empty each week, but after she starts posting sample exam questions there exclusively, the small room is standing-room only by the second week.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the students' motivation for attending office hours now?
options: They are drawn by the exclusive access to helpful exam material.
They dislike the professor's teaching style.
They attend purely to socialize with classmates.
They are required to attend by school policy.
quests.correctAnswer: They are drawn by the exclusive access to helpful exam material.
quests.hint: Think about what changed right before attendance jumped, and why that specific change would attract students.
quests.explanation: A sudden jump in attendance right after exclusive exam questions were introduced suggests students are motivated by access to that helpful material.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Routine Maintenance] The amusement park closes the classic wooden roller coaster for 'routine maintenance' during its slowest month, right after several online reviews mention it feeling rougher than in previous years.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the timing of the maintenance?
options: It happens on the exact same schedule every single year regardless of reviews.
It is completely unrelated to any reviews.
It was scheduled before the ride ever opened.
It may be connected to the recent complaints about the ride's condition.
quests.correctAnswer: It may be connected to the recent complaints about the ride's condition.
quests.hint: Think about the connection between the recent reviews and the timing of this closure.
quests.explanation: Closing for maintenance right after reviews mention roughness suggests the park's timing may be connected to those recent complaints.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Not Enough Hands] The retirement home's activity board fills up with new events after residents' families start a volunteer sign-up sheet, something the staff had wanted to do for years but never had enough hands to manage.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the earlier lack of activities?
options: The staff never wanted to plan any activities.
The families were uninvolved with the retirement home before.
The residents were never interested in activities.
It was likely due to a shortage of available staff or volunteers, not a lack of ideas.
quests.correctAnswer: It was likely due to a shortage of available staff or volunteers, not a lack of ideas.
quests.hint: Think about what 'wanted to do for years but never had enough hands' reveals about the real obstacle.
quests.explanation: Wanting more activities for years but lacking enough hands suggests the shortage of volunteers, not a lack of ideas, was the real obstacle before.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Coffee by the Final Week] The same two coworkers who clashed constantly during the project's first month are seen grabbing coffee together every morning by its final week.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the coworkers' relationship over the course of the project?
options: It grew worse over the course of the project.
It never changed from the first month.
They stopped working together entirely.
It likely improved significantly as the project progressed.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely improved significantly as the project progressed.
quests.hint: Compare how the coworkers interacted at the beginning of the project with how they interact by the end.
quests.explanation: Going from constant clashes to getting coffee together daily suggests the coworkers' relationship improved considerably as the project went on.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [The Community Fridge] The neighborhood's community fridge, stocked entirely through anonymous donations, empties completely within hours each time it is filled, and a waiting list of families now checks the group chat for updates.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the need the community fridge addresses?
options: Donations are no longer needed at all.
It meets a demand that is greater than the current supply of donations.
It is rarely used by anyone in the neighborhood.
It provides far more food than anyone needs.
quests.correctAnswer: It meets a demand that is greater than the current supply of donations.
quests.hint: Think about what emptying within hours, plus a waiting list, suggests about supply versus need.
quests.explanation: Emptying within hours and having families track a waiting list suggests the fridge addresses a need greater than what current donations can supply.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Ready, But Not Yet Shown] The clinic's online portal shows Mr. Abara's test results as 'ready,' but when he calls to ask about them, the receptionist says a doctor needs to review them with him directly before he can see the numbers.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the nature of the results?
options: They may include something the doctor wants to explain in person.
They have not actually been completed yet.
They belong to a different patient entirely.
They are completely normal and require no discussion.
quests.correctAnswer: They may include something the doctor wants to explain in person.
quests.hint: Think about why results marked 'ready' would still require a direct conversation before being shared.
quests.explanation: Needing a doctor to review 'ready' results directly, rather than letting the patient view them immediately, suggests there may be something in them worth explaining carefully.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Recalculating Total] The shopper's cart total keeps recalculating lower each time she scans her loyalty card, ultimately dropping by nearly a third of the original amount before she reaches the register.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the shopper's loyalty card?
options: It has no effect on her total at all.
It only works for a single item in her cart.
It is increasing the price of her items.
It is applying several discounts tied to her account.
quests.correctAnswer: It is applying several discounts tied to her account.
quests.hint: Think about what a lower recalculated total, right after scanning the card, suggests about what the card does.
quests.explanation: A dropping total right after scanning the loyalty card suggests the card is applying multiple discounts tied to her account.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [One Flagged Login] The password manager flags one of Mr. Duarte's saved logins as 'possibly compromised' after a data breach is reported at a company he has an account with, though none of his other saved logins are flagged.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the flagged login?
options: It is unrelated to any recent security issue.
The password manager flagged it at random.
Every one of his accounts was affected equally.
It is likely connected to the company that experienced the breach.
quests.correctAnswer: It is likely connected to the company that experienced the breach.
quests.hint: Think about why only one specific login, rather than all of them, would be flagged.
quests.explanation: Only the login tied to the breached company being flagged, while others remain unmarked, suggests that specific account is the one affected.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [The Guide Everyone Asks For] The tour company's five-star reviews mention the guide by name so often that new travelers now specifically request her when booking, even though three other guides lead similar tours.
quests.question: What can be inferred about this particular guide?
options: She is the only guide the company employs.
She receives worse reviews than the other guides.
Travelers actively avoid requesting her tours.
She has built a strong, distinct reputation among past travelers.
quests.correctAnswer: She has built a strong, distinct reputation among past travelers.
quests.hint: Think about what being requested by name, over other equally available guides, suggests about her reputation.
quests.explanation: Being requested by name over three other available guides suggests this guide has built an especially strong reputation with past travelers.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [No Nickname for the Baby] Every cousin at the reunion gets a nickname from Grandpa except for the newest baby in the family, who Grandpa insists on calling only by her full, formal name.
quests.question: What can be inferred about Grandpa's formal use of the baby's name?
options: He has simply forgotten to give her a nickname.
It may be a deliberate choice rather than an oversight.
Nicknames are something only adults receive in this family.
He dislikes the newest baby in the family.
quests.correctAnswer: It may be a deliberate choice rather than an oversight.
quests.hint: Think about whether skipping a nickname for just one person, while giving them to everyone else, seems accidental or intentional.
quests.explanation: Giving nicknames to every other cousin but deliberately using the baby's full name suggests this is likely an intentional choice, not something he simply overlooked.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Greatest Hits Outsells the New Album] The band's greatest-hits album outsells its most recent studio album by a wide margin, even though critics rated the new album higher overall.
quests.question: What can be inferred about listener behavior in this case?
options: Listeners have stopped buying music from this band entirely.
The new album is outselling the greatest-hits collection.
Critics rated the greatest-hits album higher than the new one.
Familiar, established songs are outselling the newer material.
quests.correctAnswer: Familiar, established songs are outselling the newer material.
quests.hint: Think about what a big gap in sales, despite the new album's higher reviews, suggests about what listeners are choosing.
quests.explanation: The greatest-hits album selling far more, despite lower critical reviews, suggests listeners are gravitating toward familiar songs over new material in this case.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [From One Page to Five] The onboarding checklist for new hires grows from one page to five over three years, with each addition traced back to a specific mistake made by a previous new employee.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the reason the checklist expanded?
options: New employees stopped making mistakes entirely.
It was updated in response to real problems that occurred.
It was expanded without any particular reason.
The company reduced its hiring process instead of expanding it.
quests.correctAnswer: It was updated in response to real problems that occurred.
quests.hint: Think about what tracing each addition back to an actual past mistake suggests about why the checklist grew.
quests.explanation: Each addition tracing back to a specific past mistake suggests the checklist grew specifically to prevent those same issues from happening again.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Cycling to Work] Mr. Farrow's cholesterol numbers improve at his annual check-up for the first time in five years, the same year he mentions switching from driving to cycling to work.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the connection between the two changes?
options: The two changes are certainly unrelated to each other.
His cholesterol worsened after he started cycling.
The switch to cycling may have contributed to the improved numbers.
He stopped cycling before his check-up.
quests.correctAnswer: The switch to cycling may have contributed to the improved numbers.
quests.hint: Think about what improving numbers, in the same year as a new exercise habit, suggests about a possible connection.
quests.explanation: Cholesterol improving for the first time in five years, in the same year cycling began, suggests the new habit may have played a role.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Six Members to Forty] The school's robotics club goes from six members to over forty within a year of hiring a new advisor who used to work as an engineer.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the new advisor's impact on the club?
options: The club's growth happened before she was hired.
She likely made the club more appealing or effective for students.
She discouraged students from participating.
She had no effect on how many students joined.
quests.correctAnswer: She likely made the club more appealing or effective for students.
quests.hint: Think about the timing between her hiring and the club's growth in membership.
quests.explanation: Membership growing sharply within a year of her hiring suggests the new advisor likely made the club more engaging or effective for students.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Removing the Kiosks] The grocery chain removes self-checkout kiosks from three of its busiest locations after customer surveys reveal that most shoppers there actually prefer speaking with a cashier.
quests.question: What can be inferred about shopper preferences at those specific locations?
options: They differ from what the chain may have originally assumed.
They had no opinion on checkout methods at all.
They showed universal enthusiasm for self-checkout.
They perfectly matched the chain's original expectations.
quests.correctAnswer: They differ from what the chain may have originally assumed.
quests.hint: Think about why a company would remove kiosks it presumably installed because it expected shoppers to like them.
quests.explanation: Removing kiosks after surveys reveal a cashier preference suggests actual shopper preferences differed from what the chain likely expected when installing them.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Reminder Emails in February] The soup kitchen's volunteer shifts fill up almost entirely during the holiday season, but by February, coordinators are sending reminder emails asking for anyone available to help.
quests.question: What can be inferred about volunteer patterns at the soup kitchen?
options: The soup kitchen closes every February.
February sees more volunteers than the holiday season.
Volunteer interest stays exactly the same all year.
Interest in volunteering drops noticeably after the holidays end.
quests.correctAnswer: Interest in volunteering drops noticeably after the holidays end.
quests.hint: Compare how quickly shifts fill during the holidays with the need for reminder emails afterward.
quests.explanation: Shifts filling quickly during the holidays, followed by reminder emails in February, suggest volunteer interest drops once the holiday season ends.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Under Thirty Minutes] The recipe app's most-saved dinner recipes all share one feature in common: a total preparation time listed at under thirty minutes.
quests.question: What can be inferred about what users value in a recipe?
options: Users only save dessert recipes.
Users prefer recipes that take several hours to prepare.
Preparation time has no effect on what users save.
Many users are looking for meals that can be made quickly.
quests.correctAnswer: Many users are looking for meals that can be made quickly.
quests.hint: Think about what the shared trait among the most-saved recipes reveals about a common priority.
quests.explanation: The most-saved recipes all sharing a short preparation time suggests many users prioritize meals that come together quickly.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Fewer Lost Bags] The airline's frequent complaints about lost luggage drop sharply the same quarter it switches to a new baggage-tracking system, according to the customer service department's internal report.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the new baggage-tracking system?
options: It was removed shortly after being introduced.
It made the lost luggage problem worse.
It appears to have reduced problems with lost luggage.
It was unrelated to the drop in complaints.
quests.correctAnswer: It appears to have reduced problems with lost luggage.
quests.hint: Think about the timing between the system switch and the drop in complaints.
quests.explanation: Complaints dropping sharply the same quarter the new system launched suggests the tracking system helped reduce lost luggage issues.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Visiting the Declining Stores] The new regional manager reviews every store's monthly numbers and visits only the three locations with the steepest recent declines, skipping the stores with steady or improving sales.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the manager's approach?
options: She only cares about the best-performing stores.
She plans to close every store she visits.
She is visiting stores completely at random.
She is focusing her attention on the stores that need the most support.
quests.correctAnswer: She is focusing her attention on the stores that need the most support.
quests.hint: Think about what choosing to visit specifically the declining stores, while skipping the others, suggests about her priorities.
quests.explanation: Visiting only the stores with steep declines, while skipping steady ones, suggests the manager is prioritizing the locations that most need attention.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [She Doesn't Mind] Every year, the family reunion committee asks for volunteers to organize the event, and every year, the same aunt ends up doing most of the planning by herself, mentioning she 'doesn't mind.'
quests.question: What can be inferred about the pattern of who organizes the reunion?
options: A different person organizes the event every single year.
She was formally assigned this role by a vote.
The responsibility has become an unofficial, expected role for her.
No one has ever organized the reunion successfully.
quests.correctAnswer: The responsibility has become an unofficial, expected role for her.
quests.hint: Think about what happening the same way every single year, without an official assignment, suggests about how the role became hers.
quests.explanation: The same aunt ending up in charge every year, without ever being formally assigned, suggests the role has become an unofficial expectation over time.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Wedding Season Booking] The department store's tailoring service books up three weeks in advance every wedding season, though appointments are available almost immediately during the rest of the year.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the tailoring service's busiest period?
options: It stays equally busy throughout the entire year.
It experiences much higher demand during wedding season than at other times.
It closes completely during wedding season.
It is busiest outside of wedding season.
quests.correctAnswer: It experiences much higher demand during wedding season than at other times.
quests.hint: Compare the wait times during wedding season with the wait times during the rest of the year.
quests.explanation: Booking up three weeks ahead only during wedding season, compared to immediate availability otherwise, suggests demand rises sharply during that period.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Walk After Lunch] Since Ms. Iwu began taking a short walk after lunch instead of returning straight to her desk, she reports feeling noticeably more alert during her afternoon meetings.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the after-lunch walks?
options: They are making her feel more tired overall.
They have no connection to her alertness.
They appear to be helping her feel more energized in the afternoon.
They only affect her morning energy levels.
quests.correctAnswer: They appear to be helping her feel more energized in the afternoon.
quests.hint: Think about the timing between starting the walks and noticing the change in alertness.
quests.explanation: Feeling more alert in meetings after starting the post-lunch walks suggests the walks may be helping her energy levels in the afternoon.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Sold Out at Midnight] The theater's late-night showing of the classic film sells out weeks in advance, while the same film's earlier afternoon showing on the same day still has plenty of open seats.
quests.question: What can be inferred about audience preference for this film?
options: The film is not popular at either showtime.
Both showings are equally popular.
The afternoon showing is far more popular overall.
More people are drawn to seeing it at the later showtime.
quests.correctAnswer: More people are drawn to seeing it at the later showtime.
quests.hint: Compare how quickly each showing filled up, even though it is the exact same film on the exact same day.
quests.explanation: The late-night showing selling out while the afternoon showing has open seats suggests audiences specifically prefer watching this classic film later at night.
